paite: Suangpia gam sathakten a suahsak hun uh na thei hia? ahihkeileh nou a neih lai uh na chiamteh thei hia?
english: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

paite: A chinsak zah khate na sim thei hia? Ahihkeileh a suahsak hun na thei hia?
english: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

paite: A kun ua, a tate uh a suang uh, a lungkhamnate uh a pai khia uhi.
english: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, they end their labor pains.

paite: A tate uh deihhuai takin a om ua, gamlak ah a khang lian ua; a kuankhia ua, a hongkik nawn kei uh.
english: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go forth, and don’t return again.

paite: Kuan gam sabengtung a khah khiaa? Ahihkeileh kuan gam sabengtung honte a phel a?
english: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

paite: Loupa gam a inin ka bawla, huan chi gam a tenna munin;
english: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

paite: Khopi buai nuanua a musita, hawlmi kikounate leng a za sam kei hi.
english: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

paite: Mual dungte a gantatna mun ahia, huan thilhing chiteng a zong hi.
english: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.

paite: Na na sem gingin gam bawngtal a lungkim diam? Ahihkeileh na anpiakna kiangah a omgige diam?
english: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

paite: Leilehna ah khauin gam bawngtal na khih thei diam? Ahihkeileh na nungah guamte a toktam diam?
english: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

paite: A hatna a thupi jiakin, amah na muang diam? Ahihkeileh a kiangah na sepgimna na khiat diam?
english: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

paite: Na chi in a hontuta, na buhphuala buh a kaihkhawm theihna dingin amah na muang diam?
english: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

paite: Ostrik-va kha kisathei takin a kijapa; himahleh a khavengte leh a multe a migi hia?
english: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

paite: A tuite lah leitungah a nusiaa, leivui ah a lumsaka,
english: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

paite: Khein a sikkham thei chih a mangngilha, ahihkeileh gamsain a sikgawp thei chih.
english: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

paite: Amaha hi lou bangin, a noute siatna dingin a khauha: a sep gimna bangmahlou hita zongleh, a lau kei hi:
english: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

paite: Pathian in pilna a ngolhsak jiakin, theihsiamna leng a pe sam kei hi.
english: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

paite: Tungsang lama a kitawi sang chiangin, sakol leh a tungtuangmi a nuihsan.
english: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

paite: Sakol a hatna na piak hia? Mul nemin a ngawng na tuam hia?
english: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

paite: Khaukhup bangin na tawmsak hia? A hamna thupi a lauhuai ve.
english: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

paite: Guam ah lei a tuana, a hatna ah a kipaka: mi kigalvante tuak dingin a pai khia.
english: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

paite: Lauhuai a nuihsana, a lungdong keia; namsau leng a nungngat sam kei hi.
english: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

paite: Amah ah thalbawm a ging lenglenga, teipi tezelzel leh chiangzum.
english: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

paite: Kihtakhuaina leh hehnain lei a nawmvalha; Pengkul aw ahi chih leng a um sam kei hi.
english: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

paite: Pengkul a gin tengin, Hah; a chi a, huan kidouna, heutute vanpiging leh kikou, gamlapi apan a thei.
english: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

paite: Na pilnain mu sangpi a lengsakin, a khate simlamah a phalh hia?
english: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

paite: Nang thupiakin muvanlai a tunglen in, tungsang ah a bu a sep hia?
english: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

paite: Suangpi tungah a tenga, huailaiah giahna a neia, suangpi hengte ah leh kulh muanhuaite ah.
english: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

paite: Huai akipanin matding a mu a; a miten gamla ah a mu hi.A nouten leng sisan a tep bei ua: huan thah omna mun ah, huailaiah a om hi.
english: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

paite: A nouten leng sisan a tep bei ua: huan thah omna mun ah, huailaiah a om hi.
english: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
